title: Unified Inference — Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes
author: Jordan Patel
summary: Comprehensive product document that consolidates the Unified Inference product overview, high-level PRD and requirements, design specs, roadmap & themes for the next two quarters, pricing and packaging guidance, and release notes for the initial 2027-Q1 rollout.
content:
Overview:

Unified Inference is Redwood’s unified runtime and control plane that provides a single API and operational model across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. This document consolidates the product overview, PRD-level requirements, design specification, roadmap & themes for the next two quarters, pricing and packaging guidance, and release notes for the initial 2027-Q1 rollout. It is intended for product managers, engineering leads, solutions engineering, and GTM partners.

Goals and success metrics:

- Primary goal: Deliver a single, production-grade inference experience that reduces integration complexity and lowers per-token cost for customers migrating between deployment modes.
- Success metrics (KPI):
  - Adoption: 50+ customers migrating or launching new integrations on Unified Inference within 90 days of GA.
  - Performance: p50 latency < 150ms and p95 latency < 350ms for text-generation (seq_len=512) on Hosted standard tiers.
  - Reliability: 99.90% availability SLA for Dedicated customers on monthly basis.
  - Cost efficiency: 20% reduction in per-token unit cost for targeted workloads after enabling batching + prefix caching recommendations.
  - Quality: Less than 1% of rollout-related quality regressions detected by eval sets per release window.

Target personas and use cases:

- Persona 1: Growth-stage SaaS product engineers who need a low-friction hosted API and clear upgrade path to Dedicated capacity.
- Persona 2: Enterprise platform teams requiring private deployment, strict data residency, and KMS-backed key control.
- Persona 3: ML teams optimizing latency/cost tradeoffs for high-throughput generation or embedding workloads.

High-level product capabilities (summary):

1) Single API surface for generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking with consistent request semantics.
2) Smart routing & fallback policies across hosting tiers with configurable policy rules (latency-first, cost-first, region-preferred).
3) Built-in batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization profiles surfaced in the Console and SDKs.
4) Model catalog with pinned versions and verified performance profiles for supported models.
5) Observability and cost breakdown at token/route level, integration hooks for tracing and metric exports.

PRD: Requirements (epics & representative stories)

Epic A: Unified API & SDK parity
- Requirement A1: Single REST/SDK request format supporting: generation, chat turns, function/tool calls, and streaming.
- Requirement A2: SDK parity across Python/Go/Node with consistent error types and retry semantics.
- Example story: Add streaming support to Node SDK with reconnection and idempotency token support.

Epic B: Smart routing and policy engine
- Requirement B1: Implement routing policies that evaluate request metas (latency SLO, cost budget, region, customer tier) and select target model variant.
- Requirement B2: Provide UI to author policies and an API for programmatic policy binding.
- Example story: Add a cost-first policy that routes non-interactive bulk embedding requests to quantized model variant during peak hours.

Epic C: Caching, batching, and optimizer recommendations
- Requirement C1: Automatic prefix/KV caching with consistency guarantees (TTL and versioning).
- Requirement C2: Batching engine with per-customer concurrency controls and smart batch sizing heuristics.
- Requirement C3: Redwood Optimize recommendations surfaced in the Console for quantization and batching profiles per workload.

Epic D: Deployment & security controls
- Requirement D1: Private deployment artifact (OCI bundle + Helm chart) for on-prem and VPC installs.
- Requirement D2: KMS/HSM integrations for key management and audit logging pipeline.
- Requirement D3: RBAC role matrix and support for SSO via SAML/OIDC for Enterprise customers.

Epic E: Observability, SLOs, and regression guards
- Requirement E1: Per-route telemetry (p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens-per-request, failure rates) exportable to customer destinations.
- Requirement E2: Eval harness integration to detect quality regressions tied to prompt sets and alert on drift > threshold.

Priority and non-functional requirements:

- Backwards compatibility: Existing Redwood API keys and endpoints must continue to work; new features are opt-in by default.
- Multi-region: GA in US and EU regions; APAC region as preview.
- Performance targets: p50/p95 targets listed above; memory and GPU utilization targets for Dedicated SKU documented in infra runbooks.
- Security: All traffic encrypted in transit; private deployments must support customer-managed TLS and KMS.

Design spec (architecture & key decisions)

1. Architecture overview:
- Control plane (hosted): policy engine, catalog, billing, audit logs, and UI.
- Data plane (serving runtime): GPU-optimized inference nodes organized into pools (hosted shared, dedicated reserved pools, private on-customer infra).
- Router & scheduler: Admission controller that applies routing policy and enforces concurrency & SLO-aware scheduling.

2. Key design decisions:
- Decision 1: Maintain stateless API frontends; KV cache state lives in per-customer regional cache cluster with versioning. Rationale: scales routing and simplifies failover.
- Decision 2: Model variants (quantized, fp16, small-context) are catalog entries with compatibility metadata. Router can fallback to compatible variants based on policy.
- Decision 3: Batching implemented in the runtime with per-model adaptive batch size and early flush on latency boundary.

3. API shapes & examples (representative snippets):
- POST /v1/generate
  Request sample (JSON):
  {
    "model": "redwood/unified-v1",
    "input": "Summarize the following document...",
    "stream": true,
    "policy": "latency-first",
    "trace_id": "cli-12345"
  }

  Response streaming format: chunked JSON LINES with fields: event_type, token, partial_text, usage.tokens.

4. Config & admin options (table):

| Setting | Default | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| default_routing_policy | latency-first | Used when customer does not specify policy |
| batch_max_tokens | 1024 | Upper bound per batch (can be lowered for low-latency workloads) |
| kv_cache_ttl | 24h | Customer-configurable, versioned keys |
| fallback_enabled | true | If false, requests that cannot meet policy will error |

Roadmap & themes (Q2 2027 — Q3 2027)

Themes for next two quarters:
- Theme 1: Enterprise readiness (Private GA, KMS, SSO, audit pipeline) — owner: Priya Nair
- Theme 2: Cost & performance controls (Optimize recommendations, batching defaults, quantization catalog) — owner: Sofia Martinez
- Theme 3: Developer experience (SDK parity, streaming, examples, quickstarts) — owner: Jordan Patel

Milestones and dates (high level):
- 2027-03-15: Private deployment preview (alpha) — on-prem artifact + install guide. Owner: eng-private-deployments.
- 2027-04-01: SDK parity and streaming GA for Python & Node (non-blocking for Hosted customers). Owner: eng-developer-experience.
- 2027-05-10: Routing policy editor v1 in Console + API bindings. Owner: eng-platform.
- 2027-06-01: Redwood Optimize recommendations integrated with Console for top 10 customers (pilot). Owner: eng-research.
- 2027-07-15: Dedicated SLA & reserved capacity billing integration (finance + eng-billing).

Dependencies & risks:
- Dependency: GPU capacity and availability in target regions (eng-infra). Risk: supply constraints could delay Dedicated launches; mitigation: cross-cloud pooling and burst policies.
- Dependency: KMS/HSM integrations with major cloud providers; mitigation: provide bring-your-own-KMS and dual-mode (hosted-managed) support during transition.

Pricing & packaging notes

Guiding principles:
- Keep entry-level hosted pricing simple and predictable for PLG customers.
- Offer reserved pricing for Dedicated contracts with tiered discounts for 6/12/24 month commitments.
- Separate packaging for Private deployments: platform fee + support + optional capacity commits.

Proposed pricing tiers (illustrative):
- Hosted Developer (self-serve): $0/month base, $0.004 per 1k tokens gen, $0.0006 per 1k embeddings, 30k free tokens monthly trial.
- Hosted Business: $200/month base + $0.003 per 1k tokens gen, $0.0005 per 1k embeddings, soft SLOs.
- Dedicated (Reserved pools): Custom monthly commit. Example: 1 GPU pool equivalent (A100-equivalent) starting at $12,000/month with 15% discount for annual. Includes 99.9% SLA.
- Private (on-prem / VPC): Platform license + deployment support: $50k one-time + $8k/month support + optional capacity pricing. Includes advanced compliance options.

Add-ons and enterprise options:
- Premium SLA (99.95%), extended observability retention (12 months), annual security review, and white-glove onboarding.

Billing considerations:
- Metering should align with units visible in Console: gen_tokens, embed_tokens, retries, and reserved capacity usage.
- Billing pipeline must support proration for mid-month upgrades and capacity burst credits.

Release notes: 2027-Q1 unified-inference initial rollout (v1.0.0)

Release date: 2027-03-01

Highlights:
- GA of Unified Inference API for Hosted customers with streaming, model catalog, and basic routing policies.
- Alpha for Private deployment (OCI bundle + Helm chart + install guide).
- SDK updates: Python & Node streaming parity.
- Console: per-route cost & latency breakdowns and traffic overview.

Notable fixes & improvements:
- Improved batching heuristics for short-LLM sequences that reduced p95 latency by ~12% in internal benchmarks.
- Fixed a race condition in KV-cache invalidation that could cause stale prefixes during canary rollouts.

Open issues & known limitations:
- APAC region: capacity is preview only; not recommended for production.
- Fallbacks to quantized model variants may alter generation characteristics; customers should run eval sets before enabling cost-first policies.

Rollout and runbook (deployment checklist):

1) Pre-launch: QA signoff on core metrics, security checklist complete, smoke tests in US & EU regions. Owner: eng-sre
2) Gradual rollout: Canary 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 24-hour observation windows. Owner: eng-platform
3) Monitoring: Observe p50/p95 latency, error rate > 0.5% trigger immediate rollback. Owner: oncall and eng-sre
4) Post-launch: 7-day health review + QBR summary for pilot customers. Owner: customer-success
